_readme: Canine dermatology MEDICINES — Poland. An ESTIMATE built entirely from public sources.
No public source measures this market, so every monetary figure is MODELLED, not observed.
This file is the single reproducible source for dog-derm-poland.html.
v4 (6 Aug 2026) NARROWS THE SCOPE TO MEDICINES ONLY, at the client's direction. Medicines are
now built DIRECTLY from Polish medicine prices (method 1) rather than derived as a share of a
wider total. The German transfer is RETAINED BUT REJECTED: it implies EUR 150-211 of medicine
for a simple episode, which retail prices contradict. Reported: EUR 30-80M, central EUR 60M.

TRANSFER_RULE.principle: Rates transfer across markets; money does not.
TRANSFER_RULE.why: Clinical parameters are biological and broadly stable across comparable dog populations. Economic parameters scale with income, veterinary price level, and insurance penetration — all of which differ sharply between Poland and every reference market available.

scopes.PLAIN_STATEMENT: The scope is what dog owners in Poland pay for medicines to treat skin problems in their dogs, over one year.
included: Oral antibiotics and antifungals for skin infections

context_wider_definitions.with_vet_fees_and_tests: EUR 70-150M — the same disease counted with consultation fees and tests. Medicines are 40-55% of it.
context_wider_definitions.published_market_report_definition: EUR 100-340M — adds flea/tick products, supplements and cats. NOT comparable to the headline.

fx.note: EUR/PLN ~4.30 (2024-25 band 4.2-4.4). USD/EUR ~1.08 (2024). Model is built in PLN; USD vendor figures converted at 1.08.

prevalence_ladder._warning: These four rows measure FOUR DIFFERENT OBJECTS and must never be mixed or averaged. The 74x spread between the first and second row is definitional, not geographic.

rows.note: One specific diagnosis, claims-based. A FLOOR for chronic atopic cases, not a skin-disease rate.
2nd most common disorder group. THE FIGURE USED IN THIS STUDY.
Partly overlapping with the skin group; not additive.

rows.source: Hill et al. 2006; Univ. Montreal small-animal clinic
rows.note: Share of VISITS, not share of dogs. Higher because affected dogs visit repeatedly.

reference_markets._role: Poland has no domestic prevalence or derm-market data. These four markets supply transferable rates and the scaling factors needed to move economics into Polish conditions.

poland.source: FEDIAF 2025 (2023 data); Eurostat comparative price levels 2024; pet-insurance penetration trade estimates

germany.role: PRIMARY TRANSFER SOURCE — the only reference market with a published country-level dermatology figure, which makes the backtest possible.
germany.source: Grand View Research Horizon (Germany veterinary dermatology drugs, 2024); FEDIAF; Eurostat
germany.CAVEAT: Vendor figure, unaudited. Global totals from competing vendors differ by ~2x (Grand View USD 17.4bn for 2024 vs Future Market Insights USD 9.7bn for 2025), so this anchor carries roughly +/-100% vendor uncertainty.

uk.role: PREVALENCE SOURCE — best clinical epidemiology available anywhere (VetCompass primary-care, large sample). Economics NOT transferred.

sweden.role: DEFINITIONAL CONTROL — near-universal insurance yields exceptional registry data, but its 0.17%/yr atopic-dermatitis incidence measures a narrow diagnosis, not skin disease broadly. Included to prove the prevalence ladder, not to set the rate.

czechia_hungary.role: ECONOMIC ANALOGUES — closest to Poland in income and vet-market structure. Used to confirm Poland's price level (72) sits in a coherent CEE band rather than being an outlier. Too data-thin to supply prevalence or market size.

scaling_factors._use: Applied ONLY to money transferred from a reference market into Poland. Never applied to clinical rates.

price_level_poland_vs_germany.basis: Eurostat comparative price levels: Poland 72 vs Germany ~110 on EU=100 → ratio ~0.65. Polish vet visit 100-250 PLN (EUR 23-58) vs German basic care EUR 100-250/yr corroborates.

treatment_seeking_poland_vs_germany.basis: Pet insurance penetration <10% (PL) vs ~20% (DE). Uninsured owners defer follow-ups and decline referrals, so fewer billed episodes per case — not merely cheaper ones.

method_1_direct_from_polish_prices.formula: 8.1M dogs x {8%,12%,18%} treated x {145,265,385} zl medicine cost / 4.30

medicine_cost_build.single_episode_zl: 50-150 (medicated shampoo, topical, or short oral course)
medicine_cost_build.chronic_case_zl_per_year: 1,000-2,500 (oclacitinib alone 840-1,640 at 46-90 zl per 20 tablets, plus flare-up medicines)

SENSITIVITY_chronic_share.note: The chronic share is the single most influential input in this method.

method_2_share_of_total_treatment.formula: EUR 70-150M total treatment spend x 40-55% medicine share

method_3_german_transfer_REJECTED.REJECTED_BECAUSE: Implies EUR 240-283 of medicine per treated German dog per year. Allowing 10% chronic cases at EUR 500/yr, every SIMPLE episode would need EUR 211 of medicine; at a generous 20% chronic at EUR 600 it still needs EUR 150. German and Polish retail prices for a medicated shampoo or short antibiotic course are a fraction of that.
method_3_german_transfer_REJECTED.likely_cause: The German vendor figure probably retains more OTC and preventative product than its stated 45.2% antiparasitic share implies.
method_3_german_transfer_REJECTED.supporting: Two established publishers report figures a factor of two apart for the same global market.

results.VERIFICATION_HANDLE: At the central estimate this is ~EUR 8,000 of dermatology medicine per veterinary practice per year (EUR 60M / 7,600 practices). Directly checkable against any known Polish account.

veterinary_facilities.unit: licensed animal-treatment establishments (zaklady lecznicze dla zwierzat)
veterinary_facilities.source: Krajowa Izba Lekarsko-Weterynaryjna / WetSystems register; ~72% are clinics, avg ~1.5 vets each. Business-directory counts run higher (8,800 IBISWorld; ~12,700 CompanyData) because they include all registered vet businesses.
veterinary_facilities.note: Free, public, complete national register at wetsystems.org.pl — countable by voivodeship.

supply_side.regional_concentration: Mazovia (Warsaw) ~1,691 vet businesses, Greater Poland ~850, Silesia ~666, Lower Silesia ~612 (business-directory basis).

poland_vet_services_market.source: IBISWorld Veterinary Services in Poland (~EUR 1.4bn, 2026); Ken Research (~USD 0.9-1.5bn); Eurostat production value EUR 827.6M (2023) → ~EUR 997M by 2028.
poland_vet_services_market.note: Whole veterinary market — includes farm/livestock work, not companion-animal only.

derm_share_of_canine_clinical_spend.note: Dermatology is ~15-25% of consultation VOLUME but less of REVENUE — skin visits are cheaper than surgery or dentistry.

known_breaks_and_limits: EU veterinary prices rose ~37% since 2015 and are still running ~6%/yr vs ~2% general inflation — any figure older than ~2 years understates current spend.
The top-down envelope captures clinic-channel spend only, so it structurally leans low.
Vendor country figures are unaudited and mutually inconsistent by ~2x at the global level.
No deflator applied: all figures are a single recent year (2023-2026), not a time series.
Sweden's 0.17%/yr is atopic-dermatitis incidence from insured claims — NOT comparable to the UK's 12.58% all-skin period prevalence.

paid_vendors.gives: Actual pharmaceutical sales through the vet channel and patient visits/spend by therapeutic area, monthly, by country — the only real measured source for Polish derm sales.
Country-level veterinary dermatology drug outlook (Poland cut available).
